text: A tenant in {place} ought to be able to open the lease at the kitchen table and work out how much the rent can go up. I'll vote for a limit they can use that way.
author: Codex writer B

text: Say you live across the hall from me in {place}. Your lease starts tomorrow and mine starts today. Before we put a ceiling on rent, tell us which of us gets it.
author: Codex writer B

text: If the neighbors sign around the same time, {presiding}, what date would you check to see whether the same limit covers them?
author: Codex writer B

text: When each new term begins, {presiding}. I'd want a tenant to be able to take that date and look up the applicable rule.
author: Codex writer B

text: The new term starts on the date printed on each renewal, {presiding}. I'd match each of those dates to the period the ceiling covers.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd ask for the start dates, {presiding}. Living across the hall from somebody doesn't tell you that your new lease comes under the same rule.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with when each new term begins, {presiding}. My worry is the tenant who misses the cutoff by a day and expected the same protection as the neighbor.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd put a ceiling on increases, {presiding}. When an owner tells us what it'll cost, I'd like to see what tenants have actually been paying.
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose a landlord in {place} takes the rent roll to the fuel dealer. Will the dealer deliver oil against money the tenants still owe? That's why I'm wary of setting a limit here.
author: Codex writer B

text: The owner brings in a rent roll, {presiding}. Which column would you use to tell how much money actually came in?
author: Codex writer B

text: The payments received, {presiding}. Then I'd compare that with the amounts billed before drawing conclusions about the effect of a limit.
author: Codex writer B

text: The payments column, {presiding}. A tenant could owe the highest rent the owner is allowed to charge and the building could still be a check short.
author: Codex writer B

text: Receipts, {presiding}. You can't pay the plumber with the difference between the rent on a ledger and the rent that cleared.
author: Codex writer B

text: Look for when the money came in, {presiding}. If all the owner brought was a list of charges, we still don't know how much they collected.
author: Codex writer B

text: I want some protection for renters in {place}. I can also see why somebody whose father borrows to keep his building up would come here to argue the other side.
author: Codex writer B

text: Picture coming home to your own rent bill after spending the afternoon pricing a repair for your mother's building in {place}. That's the person I want to hear before we set a limit.
author: Codex writer B

text: If a renter in {place} helps a parent run a building, can the clerk count them as favoring a rent ceiling on the strength of their address?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd put down the position the person actually gives, {presiding}. I support limits myself. That doesn't tell us where another tenant stands.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask which way they'd vote, {presiding}. They could have a renewal on their kitchen table and a roofer's estimate on their father's table.
author: Codex writer B

text: Their address tells us that they rent, {presiding}. I'd still want to hear what they think the proposal would mean for the building.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave the space blank, {presiding}. Somebody paying rent may have spent last night helping a parent figure out how to pay for repairs.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd give a family some protection at renewal even if the permitted change comes in stages. Knowing when the payment can change is worth something, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: What does a family in {place} hear when we promise a freeze? Probably that the check stays the same through the lease. I can't vote for that promise if the increase comes sooner.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could we tell a tenant that a freeze at the start of the lease lasts until they move or renew, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Show me the payment schedule, {presiding}. The first stretch can be frozen and the next payment can still go up while the family lives under that same lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd circle the month the allowance changes, {presiding}. If the freeze covers only the first part of the term, the family needs to know that before signing.
author: Codex writer B

text: Only if the schedule says the freeze runs that long, {presiding}. The tenant needs to know which month's check changes.
author: Codex writer B

text: Show me the end date, {presiding}. A family making a budget needs to know when that protection runs out.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm for letting owners set the rent again, {presiding}. The first person to renew after we vote deserves to know whether that change starts with their lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: People across the hall from each other will swap renewal notices, {presiding}. I'd keep the ceiling so each household has somewhere to look up what the owner can ask.
author: Codex writer B

text: One lease starts before repeal takes effect and the neighbor's starts afterward. Would you give those neighbors the same advice, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd keep both dates in front of me, {presiding}. Read the transition provision before saying the same rule applies to both households.
author: Codex writer B

text: Which day does the new term start? That's the first thing I'd ask a caller in {place}. I'm voting to lift the ceiling, but I can't tell them it reaches their lease without checking.
author: Codex writer B

text: Their new terms may start on opposite sides of the cutoff, {presiding}. I'd need both dates before I'd give them the same advice.
author: Codex writer B

text: Read the two leases separately, {presiding}. I'd sooner keep the protection, but if repeal carries, those families still deserve an answer that fits their own renewal.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll vote to lift the limit, {presiding}. Anybody counting on the extra rent to pay the plumber should wait until the tenant's check clears.
author: Codex writer B

text: Letting a landlord ask for more doesn't put more money in a tenant's pocket. I'd keep the limit, {presiding}, and look at the difference between bills sent and payments received.
author: Codex writer B

text: If we let an owner in {place} charge more, how much of that increase can the building spend before the tenant pays?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd count it when it's paid, {presiding}. A higher asking rent might never show up in the bank.
author: Codex writer B

text: None of the unpaid increase, {presiding}. The vote would change what the owner can ask. The rent still has to come in.
author: Codex writer B

text: A bill mailed out isn't cash coming in. Where would the tenant find the extra money, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: The owner has a balance due and somebody in {place} has another month's debt. That's what can happen when the rent goes up faster than the tenant's pay.
author: Codex writer B

text: A renter can favor more income for a parent's building and still have qualms about losing protection at home. I'd vote for repeal without putting words in that renter's mouth, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd keep the ceiling, {presiding}. If my parent owned a building with a roof that leaked, I'd still want this house to hear the repair estimate.
author: Codex writer B

text: A renter in {place} wants a bigger allowed increase for a parent's building. Did they ask us to get rid of the ceiling altogether?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd record the request for a larger allowance. If we want that person's view on repeal, {presiding}, we'd have to ask another question.
author: Codex writer B

text: No, {presiding}. They asked for more room under the limit. I'm voting to lift it, and that part is my decision.
author: Codex writer B

text: Asking to change an allowance is a position on its size, {presiding}. Ending the rule altogether is a separate vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: Record what they asked for, {presiding}. They told us a parent's costs had gone up. They never said owners should get to set any rent they choose.
author: Codex writer B

text: If we're going to repeal the limit, let's be clear about the lease already in somebody's drawer. I'd want the terms read before anybody sends out a new bill, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Imagine a family in {place} marking the frozen months on a calendar the day they sign. I'd keep the limit so they can tell what their next payment will be.
author: Codex writer B

text: A tenant's lease starts with a freeze and allows a change later on. Could you tell that family what to write on next month's check from the repeal vote alone, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: It takes the lease and the repeal's effective terms to answer that, {presiding}. The vote alone supplies no dollar amount.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask when the freeze ends and what the lease calls for afterward, {presiding}. A vote to lift the ceiling doesn't tell me what that family agreed to pay.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd read the lease before telling anybody to pay more, {presiding}. We also need to know when the repeal reaches that agreement.
author: Codex writer B

text: The family should bring in the payment schedule. Which month are they in, {presiding}, and what does the lease say that payment should be?
author: Codex writer B

text: A tenant gets the renewal in the mail before repeal and sends it back afterward. I'd end the limit, {presiding}, but which date does the tenant circle?
author: Codex writer B

text: I favor lifting the ceiling, {presiding}. Hand the first tenant who renews an explanation they can check against their own lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: In {place}, two renewals could come in the same day's mail for leases starting months apart. I'm voting to keep the ceiling. Those households have a good reason to compare notes.
author: Codex writer B

text: Keep the limit, {presiding}. Otherwise the person answering the phone needs to know exactly which renewals change before telling a household what to expect.
author: Codex writer B

text: Would a postmark settle it, {presiding}, if the owner mailed a renewal before the limit ended and the tenant signed afterward?
author: Codex writer B

text: Only if the transition provision uses the mailing date, {presiding}. I wouldn't have a clerk choose that date for us.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd keep the envelope, {presiding}, and check which date the provision actually names. A postmark can answer when something was mailed.
author: Codex writer B

text: What should we put on the notice a renter in {place} opens the week the ceiling comes off?
author: Codex writer B

text: Give them the date the change applies and show them where to find the corresponding date on a renewal. I'd want to try those instructions on a lease myself, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd show a renewal on each side of the cutoff, {presiding}. Let a tenant see which example fits before they have to call us.
author: Codex writer B

text: Lift the ceiling and an owner can ask tenants for more, {presiding}. The crew coming to patch the roof still wants a check they can cash.
author: Codex writer B

text: I favor repeal. If the question is whether a building can meet payroll, {presiding}, bring me the collections page.
author: Codex writer B

text: You've handed me a rent roll, {presiding}. Show me the payments before you say this building can carry another increase. I'm voting to keep the limit.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who's left carrying the balance, {presiding}, when a tenant can't pay the increase? I want us to answer that before we take the ceiling off.
author: Codex writer B

text: An owner in {place} says lifting the limit will cover a new boiler. Where would you look to see if there's money to pay the contractor?
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with the deposits and the invoice due date. I'm for repeal, {presiding}, but a contractor can only draw on what's there.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd ask how much came in and when the contractor expects payment, {presiding}. Lifting the ceiling won't pay an invoice that comes due before the rent.
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose the tenant pays part of the new rent. Where does the rest show up, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Enter it as rent owed, {presiding}. I'll vote to lift the ceiling, but you can't pay a repair crew with the difference between a charge and a payment.
author: Codex writer B

text: On the tenant's account as a debt, {presiding}. If we're looking at what they could afford that month, the payment tells us more than the charge.
author: Codex writer B

text: If my mother owned a building in {place}, I'd want to be able to speak up for her without the clerk deciding that I'd taken a position on my own lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll vote to let owners set the rent, {presiding}. A tenant worried about a parent's building deserves a hearing even if they'd draw the line somewhere else.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd keep a ceiling, {presiding}. A person can worry about a parent's repair bill and still want some protection when their own lease comes up.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd vote against repeal. I'd also yield my time to hear what it costs a renter's family to keep a building open, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's a space on the witness card for a position on lifting the ceiling, {presiding}. What goes there if the renter only asked for a larger increase?
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave the position open until the witness supplies it. The clerk can put the request for a larger increase in the minutes, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Give the witness their card back, {presiding}. I'm opposed to lifting the limit. That doesn't tell the clerk where the witness stands.
author: Codex writer B

text: If that renter had another minute at the microphone, {presiding}, what would you ask?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd ask whether allowing a bigger increase would cover the expense they described, {presiding}. There's a fair distance between that and letting the owner charge whatever they choose.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd ask how the change they want for their parent's building would work when their own renewal comes due. They know both sides of that question, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm voting to lift the limit, {presiding}. Before telling anyone to write a bigger check, open their lease to the page where the first increase is due.
author: Codex writer B

text: Renters in {place} may have already put the increase on their calendar. I'm ready to lift the ceiling, and I want to know where that leaves the date they wrote down.
author: Codex writer B

text: Imagine setting money aside for the later increase and finding a bigger bill in the mailbox this month. I'd keep the limit, {presiding}. What happens to the schedule that family signed?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd keep the limit, {presiding}. The tenant looking at a higher charge has to sort out whether it came from this vote or from a change already in the lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: The first higher bill comes while the lease still shows the rent frozen. What would you ask the tenant in {place} to bring in before telling them it's due?
author: Codex writer B

text: The bill, the signed schedule and the provision covering existing leases. I'd put the billing month beside the end of the freeze, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd want the dates on the bill and the agreement in front of me, {presiding}. Then I'd ask what authority the owner is relying on to charge it early.
author: Codex writer B

text: If the freeze ends the same month repeal takes effect, how would you tell what caused the higher charge, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Work it out from the signed schedule first, {presiding}. If that's exactly what the tenant was already due to pay this month, repeal didn't add the difference.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd ask for the old schedule and the owner's calculation. Which part of the charge would have appeared anyway, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Could that envelope have sat on the kitchen table for a week? The postmark tells us when the letter traveled, {presiding}. Check whether the bill uses that date or the start of the lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: Read the effective-date clause aloud, {presiding}. If it says renewals starting after a certain day, the date to look up is on the lease.
author: Codex writer B

text: Give the person opening the letter a sentence they can finish for themselves, {presiding}. My renewal starts on this date, so this is the rule that applies to me.
author: Codex writer B

text: Where in {place} can the tenant take the notice if the dates don't match their lease? Put that contact right next to the date the ceiling comes off.
author: Codex writer B

text: Has the check cleared, {presiding}? That's what the person coming down to fix the boiler needs to know.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with the balance the owner can draw on today, {presiding}. Then take out whatever's already committed to payroll and other bills. Is there enough left for the repair?
author: Codex writer B

text: Turn the ledger toward the tenant, {presiding}. The charge goes on one side and the payment on the other. That gap is what the owner still says the tenant owes.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's an unpaid balance, {presiding}, and it can follow that household into next month even if they make next month's payment in full.
author: Codex writer B

text: Whose card is it, {presiding}? Give it back to the renter and let them decide whether to mark a position.
author: Codex writer B

text: The witness asked for a larger increase, {presiding}. Put that in the minutes and leave their position on lifting the ceiling unmarked.
author: Codex writer B

text: You told us what your parent's building needs. Could we meet that need and still keep a ceiling on your own rent? That's what I'd want the witness to address, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Which expense in the building is hardest to cover right now? I'd use the extra minute on that, {presiding}, because the witness came here with some knowledge our committee could use.
author: Codex writer B

text: Bring the page both parties signed, {presiding}. Point to the month the freeze ends. Can the owner show us what permits a higher charge before that month?
author: Codex writer B

text: The envelope might have arrived early for a payment due later. Check which month the charge actually covers, {presiding}, then read the clause that applies to that month alongside the repeal provision.
author: Codex writer B

text: Cover up the new bill for a moment, {presiding}. Using just the signed lease, what would you expect this month's rent to be? Now uncover the bill and compare.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask the owner to show their work, {presiding}. How much would the tenant have owed under the old schedule that same month?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd put a limit on increases in {place}. If somebody's already paid more than the owner could charge, I want them to get the difference back.
author: Codex writer B

text: Think about the next rent day in {place}. An owner admits the last charge was too high and still sends a bill for the full amount. Who fixes the tenant's account?
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose an owner promises to credit the overpayment. What should the tenant see on the next rent statement, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: A credit of its own and a smaller amount to pay, {presiding}. Somebody opening that statement should be able to see where the overpayment went.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with what the tenant actually paid above the permitted rent, {presiding}. Can you follow that amount from the receipt to the deduction on the next statement?
author: Codex writer B

text: Where's the credit? If all they get is another bill for the usual rent, the promise hasn't done the household much good, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: The opening balance, the credit and the rent still due belong on that statement, {presiding}. Otherwise the tenant has to reconstruct the whole thing from canceled checks.
author: Codex writer B

text: What if the tenant moves out before there's another month's rent to credit, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: There's no next rent check to deduct it from, {presiding}. I'd give the departing tenant a way to get the money back at their new address.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask the family where a refund can reach them, {presiding}. A credit makes sense for the neighbor who stays. The person handing back the keys needs another option.
author: Codex writer B

text: What's a tenant who's moved away from {place} supposed to do with a credit on a closed account? They need that money for the deposit on the next place.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who's going to cut the check, {presiding}? Until there's an answer for the renter who's already gone, the promise to make people whole falls short.
author: Codex writer B

text: The rent can be paid on time in {place} while a prescription sits at the pharmacy. I support a ceiling because a landlord's ledger won't show us what that payment cost the patient.
author: Codex writer B

text: Medicine left at the counter is a reason to listen, {presiding}. Before I vote for a ceiling, show me how much of that family's next increase it would prevent.
author: Codex writer B

text: If the landlord received the full rent, where would the committee look for evidence that paying it hurt somebody, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Listen at the clinic, {presiding}. When a patient says they left a prescription at the pharmacy to make rent, a paid receipt tells only part of the story.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask what the family put off on payday, {presiding}. A member who only looks for delinquent rent could miss the tenant who's gone without medicine to stay current.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask the household and, with their permission, the person they saw for care, {presiding}. Both can tell the committee something the payment record can't.
author: Codex writer B

text: The owner can tell you when the rent came in. Who knows what the tenant gave up? The tenant does, {presiding}, if we give them room to speak.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could we hear a medical witness from {place} about a missed prescription without naming the patient on the floor?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. Ask what the patient told the witness about the choice at the pharmacy. Leave identifying details out of the public account, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask what the witness saw and what the patient told them, {presiding}. We can learn how rent figured in the decision without hearing the patient's name.
author: Codex writer B

text: Keep the patient's name out of it, {presiding}. My question for the witness is how they learned that the rent payment and the missed prescription were connected.
author: Codex writer B

text: What does naming that person add, {presiding}? The witness can tell us what happened and we can ask how the proposal would have helped.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm for a ceiling, {presiding}. If a tenant's lease already lets the owner pass on higher costs, I want them to know whether they'll be charged for that expense again.
author: Codex writer B

text: Hand an old lease from {place} to the person who keeps the books. There's an increase for higher costs already written in. Before we set another limit, which increase goes on the bill?
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose the lease already passed some of a cost increase to the tenant. How would you check whether the owner counted it again, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Set the old adjustment beside the new calculation, {presiding}. If both include the same expense, look for the part of the rule that says how much to subtract.
author: Codex writer B

text: Trace the charge from the old lease to the renewal. Which part of the increase has the tenant already paid, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd want both calculations, {presiding}, including what triggered the old clause. Matching labels on two charges wouldn't settle whether they cover the same expense.
author: Codex writer B

text: Could the owner show both charges separately on a renewal in {place}? A tenant who gets one total can't tell whether they've been billed twice for the same expense.
author: Codex writer B

text: The owner says the cost clause has been dropped. What paperwork should the tenant take home, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Put the change in writing, {presiding}. Name the clause that's coming out and when it stops applying. The tenant can take that paper back out when the next bill comes.
author: Codex writer B

text: Give the tenant a copy of the change, {presiding}. Mark the clause that came out so a new manager can't pick up the old lease and bill it again by mistake.
author: Codex writer B

text: A dated copy acknowledged the way the lease requires, {presiding}. Otherwise the owner and the tenant could leave the same conversation remembering two different rents.
author: Codex writer B

text: Look at the renewal itself, {presiding}. Does it still carry the wording that lets the owner increase the charge? A verbal assurance leaves that question open.
author: Codex writer B

text: If an owner in {place} offers to hold rents steady for a tax break, hear them out. I favor a ceiling. I also want to know what a tenant would get in that bargain.
author: Codex writer B

text: A tax break for an owner in {place} means somebody collects less revenue. Before we promise a freeze on those terms, whose budget are we asking to give up the money?
author: Codex writer B

text: How could a tenant tell whether the owner kept the promise that went with a tax break, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Give tenants the dates of the promised freeze and the rent it covers. The next demand for payment gives them something to compare with that promise, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Make the agreement available to the people who pay the rent. Without it, how would they even know their building made a deal, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Let tenants put the agreement beside a rent statement from the same month, {presiding}. They should be able to tell for themselves whether the owner kept the bargain.
author: Codex writer B

text: What good is the city's tax file to a renter who can't see it? Tell each household when the freeze starts and where to take a bill that breaks it, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Has any tax relief actually been funded, {presiding}, just because a landlord offered to freeze the rent in exchange for it?
author: Codex writer B

text: No, {presiding}. An owner can make an offer. Before promising a break on the tax bill, we have to say who has the power to grant it and what it costs.
author: Codex writer B

text: Read the tax provisions, {presiding}. If there's no relief in the text, the committee heard a proposal it still has to act on.
author: Codex writer B

text: Whose revenue is being offered, {presiding}? The landlord can speak for the building. We still need an answer from the government that collects the tax.
author: Codex writer B

text: Find the authority and the money in the legislation, {presiding}. Until then the building has made a conditional offer and the public hasn't accepted it.
author: Codex writer B

text: I put the ceiling in this bill, {presiding}. If we tell an owner to credit an overpayment, I owe the tenant who's moving an answer about how to get that money back.
author: Codex writer B

text: I wrote the repeal, {presiding}. I'll defend letting an owner charge more, but if somebody says my bill will pay for a new boiler, show me the rent that actually came in.
author: Codex writer B

text: What can the tenant put in the budget for next month, {presiding}? A ceiling that answers that question is worth voting for.
author: Codex writer B

text: Before we set a limit, {presiding}, take a pair of leases beginning on either side of the cutoff. Why should a day's difference change what those households pay?
author: Codex writer B

text: Say the fuel truck is downstairs, {presiding}, and the owner is waiting on late rent. Putting a ceiling on the next bill doesn't pay for today's delivery.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'll support a limit on increases, {presiding}. I'll also listen to a renter who's helping a parent scrape together the money for a roof.
author: Codex writer B

text: The same person can be somebody's tenant and the one a parent calls when the building needs work, {presiding}. I'd hear them before I set a ceiling.
author: Codex writer B

text: Whose position goes in the hearing record, {presiding}, if a renter speaks about a parent's repair costs and says nothing about whether to cap the rent?
author: Codex writer B

text: If a tenant hears us say the rent is frozen, they'll budget on that basis, {presiding}. Count me out unless we can say which payment stays put and for how long.
author: Codex writer B

text: When does the new lease begin, {presiding}? That's what I'd ask first. Repeal might reach one neighbor's renewal months before it reaches the other's.
author: Codex writer B

text: Which bill can an owner pay with an increase the tenant hasn't paid yet, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: None of that increase is available to spend, {presiding}. It puts a debt on the tenant's account before it puts a cent in the owner's bank.
author: Codex writer B

text: Did the witness actually ask to lift the limit, {presiding}, or did they ask us to allow enough rent to fix their parent's building?
author: Codex writer B

text: That family signed a lease with the frozen months marked out, {presiding}. I'm voting against making them wonder which payment they're supposed to send.
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose both neighbors sign on Friday. One new lease starts this month and the other starts in the fall. I'd keep the ceiling, {presiding}, and tell each household what it can expect.
author: Codex writer B

text: A tenant gets a notice about the ceiling coming off, {presiding}. What needs to be on that page for them to figure out when their own rent could change?
author: Codex writer B

text: The owner says the boiler can be replaced once the ceiling comes off. How do we know the contractor can actually get paid, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd vote to lift the ceiling, {presiding}. If the next witness is here because their mother's building needs a repair, give them time to tell us about the repair before we ask for their vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm prepared to lift the limit, {presiding}. A household that signed up for an increase later in the lease needs to know whether to change the date on the calendar.
author: Codex writer B

text: If the owner bills more during a frozen month, what papers would you want to read, {presiding}, before telling that tenant to pay?
author: Codex writer B

text: Print the cutoff date and a contact who can check a lease, {presiding}. The person opening the notice may have a renewal that doesn't fit the example we gave them.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm for a rent ceiling, {presiding}. I also want the tenant who paid too much to be able to point to an actual payment they got back.
author: Codex writer B

text: An owner makes a mistake and promises a credit. The next bill arrives for the usual amount. What happens to that tenant now, {presiding}? That's my objection.
author: Codex writer B

text: They've handed back the keys, {presiding}. They can't put a credit toward another month's rent there. A refund could go toward the deposit on the new place.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's a cost to collecting the rent that nobody put in the ledger, {presiding}. A tenant left medicine behind to pay it. That's a reason to put a limit on the next increase.
author: Codex writer B

text: Can a witness explain how paying rent affected a patient's prescription, {presiding}, while keeping the patient's name out of the minutes?
author: Codex writer B

text: Some tenants already have rent adjustments tied to costs written into their leases. Before we set a ceiling, {presiding}, tell the person doing the books what to do with that old clause.
author: Codex writer B

text: Write out the original charge and the new one separately, {presiding}. If the owner can't explain how they treated the cost already passed on to the tenant, I don't trust the total.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd pass a ceiling, {presiding}. If owners are willing to hold rents steady for tax relief, let's also find out how a renter would know their building took that deal.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who pays for the promised tax break, {presiding}? Owners have offered to freeze rents, but the local budget still has to work if we take them up on it.
author: Codex writer B
